title: Which of these pictures repeat a pattern, and why?
description: A rangoli, a flower, a butterfly, a pinwheel and a cloud appear on the board one after another. The video ends on the open question of which pictures repeat their parts in a pattern, and why they please the eye.
teaching_notes: One idea: some pictures repeat a part in a definite pattern and some do not. Ask every child to guess which ones repeat, and do not confirm any guess, because the next topic settles it. Watch for students who say a picture repeats only because it is colourful.

video_script.why: Before any word of symmetry, the child notices that some pictures repeat a part in a pattern and a cloud does not, and wonders why.
video_script.substitution: Look at the rangoli, flower, butterfly, pinwheel and cloud of the chapter opener and ask which ones repeat a pattern.
video_script.anchor: The book's opening pictures: a rangoli, a flower, a butterfly, a pinwheel and a cloud
hold_back: which pictures repeat a pattern: all but the cloud
never_show: any tick or cross on a picture
the word symmetry as a definition
maths_rules: Five pictures are shown: a rangoli, a flower, a butterfly, a pinwheel and a cloud.
No fold line, no label and no number is drawn on any picture.
The open question: which pictures repeat their parts in a pattern, and why they please the eye. It is never answered or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: some pictures repeat a part in a pattern, one does not. Assumes nothing. Pictures arrive one after another and all stay to the end; the book's own five pictures, no invented scene.
